_note: Career Fit Quiz (shown after the top 5 careers). Round 1: 6 interest questions - each option is one Holland RIASEC type and every type appears 3 times. Round 2: one 'day in the job' scenario per recommended career; points = one value per option (10 best, 5 reasonable, 0 weak). The quiz helps the student choose among the 5; it never changes the trained ranking.

interest_questions.question: On a free afternoon, which would you pick?

options.text: Fix or build something with my hands
Solve a puzzle or find out how something works
Draw, design or write something of my own

interest_questions.question: In a group project, which part do you volunteer for?

options.text: Leading the group and presenting the work
Organising the plan, files and deadlines

interest_questions.question: Which job task sounds best to you?

options.text: Setting up equipment, machines or systems
Teaching, guiding or caring for people
Keeping records accurate and well organised

interest_questions.question: Which compliment would make you proudest?

options.text: "You found the answer nobody else could."

interest_questions.question: Where would you most like to work?

options.text: Outdoors, on a site or in a workshop or lab
Among people: a school, clinic or community
A busy office where I make decisions

interest_questions.question: What would you enjoy learning next?

options.text: How data or science explains the world

software_engineer.scenario: Users report that the app crashes when they upload a photo. You cannot reproduce it on your own computer.
options: Restart the server and hope it stops
Ask for the device, steps and error logs, then reproduce it and write a test for it
Tell users to stop uploading photos
software_engineer.why: Good engineers collect evidence first (steps, logs, device), reproduce the bug and add a test so it never comes back.

software_engineer.scenario: A teammate's pull request works, but the code is hard to read and has no tests.
options: Leave polite, specific comments and suggest adding tests
Approve it quickly so the team is not slowed down
Rewrite all of it yourself without telling them
software_engineer.why: Code review is teamwork: clear, respectful comments improve the code and help your teammate learn.

software_engineer.scenario: You finished a new API endpoint one day before the deadline.
options: Start the next feature immediately
Explain it only when someone asks
Write a short README and examples so others can use it
software_engineer.why: Short documentation saves the whole team time. Starting the next task is fine, but undocumented code slows others down.

data_analyst.scenario: Monthly sales suddenly dropped 40% in your dashboard.
options: Report the drop to management immediately
Check the data source and missing records first, then explain the cause
Delete that month from the chart
data_analyst.why: A sudden change is often a data problem. Checking the data before reporting avoids wrong decisions.

data_analyst.scenario: A manager with no technical background asks what your analysis found.
options: Show one clear chart and three key points in simple words
Send the full spreadsheet with all formulas
Explain the statistical tests in detail
data_analyst.why: Analysts must turn numbers into a simple story the audience can act on.

data_analyst.scenario: Your dataset has many duplicate and blank rows.
options: Use it as it is
Remove everything that looks strange
Clean it with clear rules and record what you changed
data_analyst.why: Data cleaning should follow clear, written rules so the results can be trusted and repeated.

business_analyst.scenario: Two departments want opposite features in the new system.
options: Pick the department you like more
Meet both, find the real needs behind the requests and suggest a solution
Build both features without asking
business_analyst.why: Business analysts find the real problem behind each request and help people agree.

business_analyst.scenario: Developers keep asking what a requirement means.
options: Rewrite it as a clear user story with acceptance criteria
Tell them to guess
Explain it again verbally each time
business_analyst.why: Clear written requirements (user stories and acceptance criteria) prevent repeated confusion.

business_analyst.scenario: Management asks whether a new process actually saved time.
options: Say yes because everyone seems happy
Run a staff survey only
Compare the time taken before and after using real records
business_analyst.why: Decisions should be based on evidence. A survey helps, but real before/after data is stronger.

options: Make every button bigger
Watch a few users try it, then test a clearer design
Add a long instruction text
ui_ux_designer.why: UX design starts with observing real users, then testing a fix.

ui_ux_designer.scenario: The client wants the app to look 'modern' but cannot explain more.
options: Show 2-3 mood boards and quick sketches to choose a direction
Copy a popular app exactly
Use only your favourite colours
ui_ux_designer.why: Showing options early turns a vague wish into a clear direction.

ui_ux_designer.scenario: A developer says your design is too hard to build before the deadline.
options: Insist on the original design
Let the developer change it however they like
Discuss together and simplify it while keeping the main user goal
ui_ux_designer.why: Designers and developers find a balance that keeps the user experience good and the deadline realistic.

qa_engineer.scenario: A bug appears only sometimes when you test the login page.
options: Ignore it because it is rare
Try different inputs, browsers and timings to find the pattern
Mark the test as passed
qa_engineer.why: Intermittent bugs are found by changing one condition at a time until the pattern appears.

qa_engineer.scenario: You found a serious bug and need to report it.
options: Write the steps, expected vs actual result, screenshots and severity
Send a message saying 'login is broken'
Fix the code yourself without reporting
qa_engineer.why: A good bug report lets a developer reproduce and fix the bug quickly.

qa_engineer.scenario: The release is tomorrow, but two medium bugs are still open.
options: Hide the bugs to avoid delaying
Block the release without explaining
Explain the risks to the team so they can decide
qa_engineer.why: QA gives clear information about risk; the team then makes an informed decision.

cybersecurity_analyst.scenario: Staff received an email asking them to 'confirm their password' on a strange website.
options: Do nothing because it is only an email
Warn staff, block the link and check who already clicked it
Delete your own copy only
cybersecurity_analyst.why: Phishing needs a quick response: warn, block and find affected users.

cybersecurity_analyst.scenario: You see hundreds of failed logins for one account at 2 a.m.
options: Investigate the source, lock the account and alert the owner
Assume the user forgot their password
Turn off the logging
cybersecurity_analyst.why: Many failed logins can be a brute-force attack. Investigate and protect the account.

options: Shout at them in a meeting
Write a 40-page policy nobody reads
Run short, friendly training and turn on multi-factor authentication
cybersecurity_analyst.why: Security improves with simple training and good technical controls such as MFA.

network_engineer.scenario: One office floor has no internet, but the others work.
options: Restart every device in the building
Check the switch, cables and settings for that floor step by step
Wait until tomorrow
network_engineer.why: Narrowing the problem down to the affected area is faster and safer.

network_engineer.scenario: You changed the router settings to fix an issue.
options: Record the change, the reason and how to undo it
Remember it yourself
Tell one colleague
network_engineer.why: Recording changes makes the network easier to fix later and is standard practice.

network_engineer.scenario: The company wants guest Wi-Fi for visitors.
options: Give visitors the staff Wi-Fi password
Refuse guest Wi-Fi
Create a separate guest network isolated from staff systems
network_engineer.why: A separate, isolated guest network keeps company systems safe.

database_administrator.scenario: A report query that used to take 2 seconds now takes 2 minutes.
options: Buy a bigger server immediately
Look at the query plan and add a suitable index
Tell users to run it at night
database_administrator.why: Checking the query plan finds the real cause; more hardware is expensive and may not help.

database_administrator.scenario: Your manager asks if the database could be restored after a disaster.
options: Test restoring the latest backup on a separate server
Say yes without checking
Make one copy on your laptop
database_administrator.why: A backup is only useful if it can be restored, so test it regularly.

database_administrator.scenario: A developer needs read access to customer data for testing.
options: Give full admin access
Email them the whole database
Give read-only access to masked test data and record the approval
database_administrator.why: Give the minimum access needed and protect personal data.

project_manager.scenario: The project is two weeks behind schedule.
options: Hide it from the client
Find the cause, re-plan with the team and inform the client early
Ask everyone to work every night
project_manager.why: Good project managers are honest, find the cause and re-plan together.

project_manager.scenario: The client asks for a big new feature in the middle of the project.
options: Explain the impact on time and cost and agree on a decision
Accept it without changing the plan
Refuse without discussion
project_manager.why: Scope changes are managed by showing the impact and agreeing together.

project_manager.scenario: Two team members keep arguing in meetings.
options: Remove one from the project
Ignore it
Talk to them, understand the issue and agree on clear roles
project_manager.why: Managers handle conflict early by listening and clarifying roles.

digital_marketing_executive.scenario: An ad gets many clicks but almost no sales.
options: Spend more money on the same ad
Check the landing page and who is clicking, then test changes
Stop all advertising
digital_marketing_executive.why: Marketers use data to find where people drop off and test improvements.

digital_marketing_executive.scenario: You need a social media post for a new product launch.
options: Create a short, eye-catching post that shows the benefit for the customer
Copy a competitor's post
Write a long technical description
digital_marketing_executive.why: Good marketing content is short, original and focused on the customer.

digital_marketing_executive.scenario: A customer posts an angry comment about late delivery.
options: Delete the comment
Argue publicly
Reply politely, apologise and move the details to a private message
digital_marketing_executive.why: A calm, public reply protects the brand and helps the customer.

civil_engineer.scenario: During construction you notice cracks in a newly poured concrete slab.
options: Cover them with paint
Stop work in that area, inspect the cause and consult the design team
Continue to stay on schedule
civil_engineer.why: Safety comes first: investigate structural issues before continuing.

civil_engineer.scenario: The contractor changed a material without approval.
options: Record it, check whether it meets the specification and report it
Accept it because it is cheaper
Ignore it
civil_engineer.why: Engineers keep records and make sure materials meet the approved specification.

civil_engineer.scenario: Heavy rain is forecast for the week you planned to pour the foundations.
options: Pour anyway
Cancel the project
Agree a new schedule with the site team and protect the work area
civil_engineer.why: Planning around weather with the team protects quality and safety.

options: Turn it off and on again
Check cooling, load and maintenance records to find the cause
Increase its speed
mechanical_engineer.why: Root-cause analysis (cooling, load, maintenance) fixes the problem for good.

mechanical_engineer.scenario: You must reduce the weight of a part without making it weaker.
options: Test new shapes or materials with CAD and simulation
Use a thinner part and hope
Keep the same design
mechanical_engineer.why: Engineers explore design options and test them before building.

mechanical_engineer.scenario: A technician asks how to service the new pump you designed.
options: Explain it once on the phone
Tell them to work it out
Prepare a clear maintenance guide with drawings
mechanical_engineer.why: Written guides with drawings make maintenance safe and repeatable.

electrical_engineer.scenario: A circuit breaker in a building keeps tripping.
options: Replace it with a bigger breaker
Measure the load and check the wiring for faults
Tape the switch on
electrical_engineer.why: A tripping breaker is a warning. Find the overload or fault; never bypass it.

electrical_engineer.scenario: A colleague wants to work on a panel without switching off the power to save time.
options: Insist on isolating the power and following lock-out procedures
Let them, they are experienced
Leave the site
electrical_engineer.why: Electrical safety procedures protect lives and are never skipped.

electrical_engineer.scenario: The client wants to reduce electricity costs.
options: Tell them to use fewer lights
Recommend the most expensive system
Study their usage and suggest options such as solar or efficient lighting with savings estimates
electrical_engineer.why: Good engineers analyse the usage and compare options with costs and benefits.

research_assistant.scenario: Your results do not support the hypothesis your supervisor expected.
options: Change the data so it fits
Report the results honestly and check the method
Delete the results
research_assistant.why: Research integrity means reporting results honestly, even unexpected ones.

research_assistant.scenario: You are collecting survey data from 200 people.
options: Use a clear data sheet, label every variable and back it up
Keep notes in your head
Store it in random files
research_assistant.why: Organised, backed-up data makes analysis reliable and repeatable.

research_assistant.scenario: You need to compare the test scores of two student groups.
options: Compare only the highest scores
Guess by looking at the numbers
Use a suitable statistical test and report the averages and the spread
research_assistant.why: A proper statistical test shows whether a difference is real or just chance.

laboratory_technician.scenario: You notice a sample label is unclear.
options: Guess which sample it is
Set it aside, report it and follow the lab's procedure
Throw it away quietly
laboratory_technician.why: Accurate labelling is essential. Uncertain samples must be reported, not guessed.

laboratory_technician.scenario: Your test results look very different from usual.
options: Check the equipment calibration and controls, then repeat the test
Report them anyway
Change the numbers to normal values
laboratory_technician.why: Unusual results should be checked (calibration and controls) before reporting.

laboratory_technician.scenario: A colleague is not wearing gloves when handling chemicals.
options: Say nothing
Report them without speaking to them
Politely remind them of the safety rules
laboratory_technician.why: Everyone shares responsibility for lab safety; a friendly reminder comes first.

finance_analyst.scenario: This month's expenses are 25% above the budget.
options: Increase the budget
Break the expenses down by category to find the cause
Ignore it until the year end
finance_analyst.why: Variance analysis finds which costs went over and why.

finance_analyst.scenario: You present a financial forecast to the board.
options: Show the key numbers, the assumptions and the risks clearly
Show 50 pages of tables
Show only the good news
finance_analyst.why: Decision makers need clear key figures, assumptions and risks, not only good news.

finance_analyst.scenario: A payment record does not match the bank statement.
options: Adjust the figure so it matches
Ask the bank to change its statement
Trace the transaction and find the difference
finance_analyst.why: Reconciliation means finding the real difference, never forcing the numbers.

hr_executive.scenario: An employee tells you privately they feel bullied by their manager.
options: Tell the manager immediately in public
Listen, keep it confidential and follow the grievance procedure
Tell them to ignore it
hr_executive.why: HR handles complaints fairly, confidentially and by the correct procedure.

hr_executive.scenario: A department needs to hire quickly.
options: Agree the role needs with the manager and use a fair interview process
Hire the first person who applies
Hire a friend
hr_executive.why: Fair, structured hiring finds the right person and avoids bias.

hr_executive.scenario: Staff keep asking the same questions about leave rules.
options: Answer each email separately
Stop answering
Create a simple FAQ and share it on the intranet
hr_executive.why: A clear FAQ saves time and gives everyone the same correct information.

public_health_assistant.scenario: Dengue cases are rising in a village.
options: Only put up a poster in English
Run an awareness session on removing standing water, in the local language
Wait for the hospital to act
public_health_assistant.why: Clear education in the community's language helps prevent the spread.

public_health_assistant.scenario: You collect weekly case numbers from clinics.
options: Record them in a table and look for trends by area
Keep them on paper only
Report only the total
public_health_assistant.why: Tracking trends by area shows where action is needed.

public_health_assistant.scenario: A school wants to run a health camp.
options: Do it alone
Tell them it is not your job
Plan it with teachers, health staff and parents
public_health_assistant.why: Public health work depends on partnerships with the community.

health_administrator.scenario: Patients wait over three hours at the outpatient clinic.
options: Add more chairs
Study the patient flow and change the appointment system
Tell patients to come later
health_administrator.why: Analysing the process fixes the cause of the delay, not only the symptom.

health_administrator.scenario: The hospital is moving to electronic patient records.
options: Plan training, a test run and data protection rules
Switch everything overnight
Keep paper records only
health_administrator.why: Change needs planning, staff training and protection of patient data.

health_administrator.scenario: Nurses complain about unfair shift schedules.
options: Ignore it
Let each nurse choose any shift
Meet them, review the schedule rules and create a fair rota
health_administrator.why: Leaders listen and create fair, clear rules.

graphic_designer.scenario: A client asks for a logo for a new eco-friendly café.
options: Use a free template
Research the brand, sketch several ideas and present the best
Use your favourite font
graphic_designer.why: Strong designs come from understanding the brand and exploring ideas.

graphic_designer.scenario: The client says 'I don't like it' without explaining why.
options: Ask specific questions about colours, style and feeling
Start again from nothing
Argue that the design is good
graphic_designer.why: Asking specific questions turns vague feedback into clear changes.

graphic_designer.scenario: The design must work on a website and on a large banner.
options: Send a small JPG
Ask the printer to resize it
Create vector files and versions for print and web
graphic_designer.why: Vector files and the right formats keep designs sharp everywhere.

content_creator.scenario: Your videos are getting fewer views.
options: Post the same video again
Look at audience data and try new formats and topics
Buy fake followers
content_creator.why: Creators learn from their audience data and experiment with new ideas.

content_creator.scenario: A brand offers to pay you to promote their product.
options: Accept only if it fits your audience and clearly mark it as sponsored
Promote it without saying it is paid
Promote anything that pays
content_creator.why: Honest, clearly marked sponsorships keep your audience's trust.

content_creator.scenario: You want to use music in your video.
options: Use any popular song
Lower the volume so nobody notices
Use licensed or copyright-free music
content_creator.why: Respecting copyright avoids takedowns and legal problems.

content_writer.scenario: You must write an article about a health topic you know little about.
options: Copy text from a website
Read trusted sources, take notes and write in your own words
Write from your own opinion
content_writer.why: Good writers research trusted sources and never plagiarise.

content_writer.scenario: Your article is accurate but long and hard to read.
options: Use headings, short paragraphs and simple words
Add more details
Make the font smaller
content_writer.why: Clear structure and simple language make content easy to read.

content_writer.scenario: The editor sends many comments on your draft.
options: Ignore the comments you disagree with
Rewrite everything
Go through each comment, edit and explain any you disagree with
content_writer.why: Professionals handle feedback carefully and discuss points respectfully.

public_relations_executive.scenario: A false rumour about your company is spreading online.
options: Stay silent
Quickly share a clear, factual statement
Attack the people sharing it
public_relations_executive.why: In a crisis, a fast, factual statement protects the organisation's reputation.

public_relations_executive.scenario: You need media coverage for a charity event.
options: Write a press release with a human story and contact relevant journalists
Send a generic email to all journalists
Hope they notice
public_relations_executive.why: A strong story sent to the right journalists gets coverage.

public_relations_executive.scenario: The CEO must give a TV interview tomorrow.
options: Let the CEO improvise
Cancel the interview
Prepare key messages and practise likely questions with the CEO
public_relations_executive.why: PR teams prepare spokespeople with key messages and practice.

teacher.scenario: Half the class did not understand today's lesson.
options: Move on to the next topic
Explain it again in a different way with examples and check understanding
Give extra homework
teacher.why: Good teachers check understanding and try a different approach.

teacher.scenario: A student keeps disturbing the class.
options: Talk to them privately to understand the reason and agree on expectations
Shout at them
Send them out every day
teacher.why: Understanding the reason behind behaviour works better than punishment alone.

options: Read from the textbook
Skip the topic
Use a game, a real-life example or a group activity
teacher.why: Active, real-life learning keeps students interested.

education_coordinator.scenario: Teachers are not using the new curriculum.
options: Send a strict memo
Run training, ask what support they need and follow up
Do nothing
education_coordinator.why: Change succeeds with training, support and follow-up.

education_coordinator.scenario: Exam results in one subject dropped this year.
options: Compare results by class and topic to find where learning dropped
Blame the students
Change the exam
education_coordinator.why: Analysing results by class and topic shows where support is needed.

education_coordinator.scenario: You are organising a school-wide workshop.
options: Plan it in your head
Ask people on the day
Make a written plan with dates, roles and resources and share it
education_coordinator.why: A shared written plan keeps everyone coordinated.

legal_assistant.scenario: A court filing deadline is in two days and one document is missing.
options: Submit without it
Tell the lawyer immediately and request the document
Wait until the last day
legal_assistant.why: Deadlines are critical in law, so raise problems early.

legal_assistant.scenario: The lawyer asks you to find past cases similar to the current one.
options: Search legal databases and summarise the relevant cases
Search only the first web result
Guess based on memory
legal_assistant.why: Legal research uses reliable databases and clear summaries.

legal_assistant.scenario: A friend asks about a client's case.
options: Tell them a little
Share it if they promise not to tell
Politely refuse because client information is confidential
legal_assistant.why: Client confidentiality is a core legal duty.

compliance_officer.scenario: You find a department is not following a data-protection rule.
options: Ignore it if nothing went wrong
Document it, explain the risk and agree a fix with a deadline
Report them to the media
compliance_officer.why: Compliance means finding issues, explaining the risk and fixing them.

compliance_officer.scenario: A new regulation affects how the company stores customer data.
options: Summarise what changes for each team and train them
Email the full law text
Wait for an inspection
compliance_officer.why: Staff need a clear summary of what to do differently.

compliance_officer.scenario: An auditor asks for proof that staff completed training.
options: Say everyone did it
Create records quickly now
Show the training records and attendance logs
compliance_officer.why: Accurate records are the evidence of compliance; never create false ones.

community_development_officer.scenario: You want to start a project to improve clean water in a village.
options: Decide the project yourself
Meet the villagers first to understand their needs and ideas
Copy a project from another country
community_development_officer.why: Community projects work best when the community helps plan them.

community_development_officer.scenario: Volunteers are losing interest in the project.
options: Recognise their work, give clear roles and share progress
Replace them all
Continue alone
community_development_officer.why: Recognition, clear roles and visible progress keep volunteers motivated.

community_development_officer.scenario: A donor asks what impact their funding had.
options: Say it went well
Ask for more money
Share a short report with numbers, photos and stories
community_development_officer.why: Clear impact reports build trust with donors.

counselling_assistant.scenario: A student comes to you upset and starts crying.
options: Tell them to calm down
Listen calmly, show empathy and let them speak
Give advice immediately
counselling_assistant.why: Active, empathetic listening is the first step in counselling.

counselling_assistant.scenario: A student says something that suggests they may harm themselves.
options: Follow the safeguarding procedure and involve the qualified counsellor
Keep it secret as they asked
Ignore it
counselling_assistant.why: Safety comes before confidentiality: follow safeguarding procedures.

counselling_assistant.scenario: After a session you need to write notes.
options: Write them in a shared notebook
Post them in a group chat
Write factual notes and store them securely
counselling_assistant.why: Counselling notes must be factual and stored securely.
